transcript.text: theres water in the bottom of my frige under the salad draws, keeps comming back after i mop it up

Water pooling under the salad drawers is almost always caused by a blocked defrost drain. When the fridge cycles off, frost melts into this drain; if it's clogged with food debris or gunk, the water has nowhere to go and backs up onto the shelf base. Please check the bottom rear wall of the fridge section for that small hole, clear it gently with warm water if blocked, and let me know if that stops the water returning.
ok thanks, ive never heard of a drain hole in a fridge tbh. where abouts is it exactly and what does it look like? happy to have a poke with a cotton bud if thats ok

It's usually a small hole or a narrow channel located at the very bottom of the back wall inside the fridge section. It might be hidden under a plastic cover that pops off gently, but often it's just an open drain in the base. Please check if you can see it and whether it looks blocked with food debris or ice.

ok found it, theres a little groove and a hole at the bottom of the back wall and its got bits of lettuce and gunk in it. water is only inside the fridge not on the floor or near the plug btw. should i clear it with a cotton bud and warm water?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain hose]
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes, please clear it with warm water. A cotton bud will help remove the gunk from the hole itself, but you also need to flush the tube behind it; pour a small jug of warm water into the drain until it runs freely out the back. This suggests the blockage is the cause. To check if there are any model-specific parts or recalls later, could you tell me the make and model number? It's usually on a sticker inside the fridge.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok will do. the model number on the sticker inside the fridge is CFG1582W, its a Beko. do i really need to unplug it just to poke a cotton bud in the hole?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain hose]
You don't need to unplug it just to use a cotton bud on the hole itself; you only need to unplug if you are pouring water or doing anything that risks getting liquid near electrical parts. Please clear it with the cotton bud and then flush it gently with warm water from a jug or bottle until it runs freely out the back of the fridge. This is probably the cause, but because I can't confirm the exact internal layout for your Beko model, if the water returns after this clean, you'll need an engineer to check the drain tube further down.
